property_summary: For any recipient, after calling getFirstWithdrawalBonus(recipient) a subsequent withdrawReward(recipient) must pay nothing extra because the reward was zeroed — total Ether drained from the contract is exactly 100; the mutant skips zeroing so the follow-up withdrawal pays 100 again, draining 200.

For any recipient, after getFirstWithdrawalBonus(recipient) completes (with the contract funded), rewardsForA[recipient] has been zeroed, so a follow-up withdrawReward(recipient) pays nothing and the contract's balance drops by exactly the bonus (100 wei); the mutant skips the zeroing, so the follow-up withdrawal pays 100 again and the balance drops by 200.

For any codeless recipient, once getFirstWithdrawalBonus(recipient) has paid the 100-wei bonus, a subsequent withdrawReward(recipient) must pay nothing (the reward was zeroed), leaving address(c).balance unchanged; the mutant skips zeroing so the follow-up withdrawal pays 100 wei again, changing the balance.

After getFirstWithdrawalBonus(recipient), the reward must be zeroed, so a subsequent withdrawReward(recipient) pays nothing and address(c).balance is unchanged; the mutant skips zeroing so the follow-up withdrawal pays 100 wei again.

For any codeless recipient, after getFirstWithdrawalBonus has paid the 100-wei bonus once, a second withdrawReward(recipient) must pay nothing (reward zeroed) leaving address(c).balance unchanged; the mutant skips zeroing so the second withdrawal pays 100 wei again.

For any address, calling getFirstWithdrawalBonus once (with the contract funded) must transfer exactly 100 wei of rewards out of the contract; the mutant always sends 0, so the contract's balance never decreases.

For any caller, calling getFirstWithdrawalBonus on a recipient whose fallback reverts must itself revert in C, because the 100-wei reward payout to that recipient fails; the mutant always sends 0 wei, the low-level call to the reverting recipient succeeds, and getFirstWithdrawalBonus completes without reverting.

For every recipient and caller, once getFirstWithdrawalBonus(recipient) completes on a contract holding exactly the 100-wei reward, the 100 wei must have been transferred out so that address(c).balance becomes 0; the mutant sends 0 wei, leaving the contract still holding 100 wei, violating the rule.

For any funding amount, calling getFirstWithdrawalBonus always completes successfully even when the recipient re-enters getFirstWithdrawalBonus (the reentrancy guard makes the nested call fail harmlessly), whereas the buggy version without '_locked = true' re-enters unboundedly until gas exhaustion so the outer call reverts for some inputs.

For any contract that claims the first-withdrawal bonus and re-enters at least twice, the reentrancy guard must make the outer getFirstWithdrawalBonus revert; deleting '_locked = true' lets the nested claims succeed and the outer call complete instead.

For any address, repeated withdrawal attempts must each succeed because the reentrancy lock is always released after each call; in the buggy version the lock stays set, so any subsequent withdrawReward reverts.
